correctness.rationale: The induced degree of a_i in an A∪B face is |B|−1_{b_i∈B}; the symmetric constraints give exactly the displayed mixed face types. In the sequential pivot matching, the nonempty B-fibers of size one or two are cones in the allowed A-subsets and the earlier nonapex toggles preserve apex stability. After A-stages only a_0 and pure B-faces of size at least three survive; the last pivot leaves the specified triples. On a directed cycle up and down steps must alternate (ups cannot be consecutive and the numbers agree), so every face of the cycle is matched on a cycle up-step. The earliest used pivot cannot then be deleted by a down-step whose endpoints both survived to that stage. This verifies the integral Morse wedge. Independently, a good cover by the two side simplices and the four-vertex simplices indexed by unordered pairs has nerve the suspension of the complex of families of pairs sharing an index. The latter has a good cover by index stars with nerve the one-dimensional complete graph K_n. The suspension gives the same wedge rank. The connected bipartite graph has its parts unique up to exchange, and the paired nonedges force simultaneous index permutations. For the mixed fixed simplices the sign is positive except for fixed mixed edges under part exchange, where it is negative. The reduced Lefschetz counts give (−1)^s((f²−3f+2)/2−t), the rational exterior-square character. The argument includes n=3 and makes no equivariant homotopy assertion. The frozen code and recorded finite Morse and character checks were read, not executed.

value.rationale: The full homotopy type and action on top homology for the canonical family formed by deleting a perfect matching are natural structural questions. The proof identifies why only degree-two spheres survive and the signed symmetry module explains how both part-preserving symmetries and exchange act. This is mathematically useful family-level structure, not merely a table of ranks, even though the originality comparison shows it is covered elsewhere.
